page: Microsoft Azure D48pds_v5 is a general-purpose server belonging to the DPDSv5 family, powered by an Ampere Altra ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 processor. It features 48 physical ARM64 cores running at 3.0 GHz with a 1:1 thread-to-core ratio, providing dedicated CPU resources without hyperthreading. The hardware configuration includes 192.0 GB of RAM, translating to 4.0 GB of memory per core, and is equipped with 1843 GB of local SSD storage. It is also Premium Storage capable and runs under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong multi-core performance, with stress-ng multi-core CPU testing scoring 85110.68 and Geekbench software compilation with Clang reaching 39488.0. Redis SET operations are highly efficient, processing 61.96 million operations per second. However, single-core capabilities are more moderate, as evidenced by an average single-core stress-ng score of 1822.49 and a weak Geekbench single-core score of 1121.0. Memory bandwidth is stable, recording 175.53 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 76.31 GB/sec for large-block writes.

The ARM64 architecture of the D48pds_v5 offers a cost-efficient alternative to traditional x86 architectures by delivering high physical core density and dedicated resource allocation at a lower qualitative cost profile. Given its balanced 1:4 memory-to-vCPU ratio and substantial 1843 GB local storage, this server is well-suited for multi-threaded workloads, database operations, Redis caching layers, and software compilation tasks. It is less optimal for single-threaded processing or heavy large-model LLM inference.
